name: setup_vscode_debug_config
description: Local/dev-testing only -- never relevant to a real production install. Call this AFTER a successful install_generated_plugin (needs the plugin's real, host-assigned profileNum to find its /usr/local/etc/rc.d service script). Writes a .iox_env file into this plugin's own directory, containing the exact PG3INIT value the real daemonized process uses (copied verbatim from its rc.d script), and a .vscode/launch.json with one debugpy 'launch' entry (named after the plugin, program main.py, envFile pointing at .iox_env, justMyCode false) so the plugin can be attached to and debugged directly from VS Code with the same PG3/MQTT identity the real service uses. Always overwrites both files -- PG3INIT rotates on every real restart, so re-calling this after a restart is expected and safe. Also refreshes OS permissions on these files once after both are written -- a hub-side failure there is reported back as a non-fatal 'permissions_refresh_error' field and never means the files weren't written. This also notifies the platform of both files written -- a hub-side failure there is reported back as a non-fatal 'files_changed_notify_error' field and never means the change itself failed. Before any of that, this also checks whether the hub's VS Code Remote setup (installing missing packages, configuring the environment) has already been done -- tracked once for the whole plugin output root, not per plugin. If it hasn't (or 'force' is set), this call returns early with {"stage": "vscode_remote_confirm", "needs_confirmation": true, "question": ...} instead of doing anything else -- relay that question to the human verbatim and wait for their answer, then call this tool again with the same 'location' plus 'confirm_vscode_remote' set to true or false based on their reply. Only once 'confirm_vscode_remote' is set does this call actually proceed (to VS Code Remote setup if true, or straight past it if false, either way then doing the normal .iox_env/.vscode/launch.json write described above). The result then includes a 'vscode_remote' field: {"attempted": false} if they said no, or {"attempted": true, "succeeded": bool, ...} if setup ran -- on success this also includes 'instructions' (steps plus an ssh_config_snippet for the human's local ~/.ssh/config, using the hub's real detected IP/name) for attaching VS Code's Remote-SSH extension to this hub; on failure it includes an 'error' instead, and the outcome is remembered so the next call asks again. Pass 'confirm_vscode_remote' only on that follow-up call, never speculatively.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root -- the same 'location' generate_plugin_scaffold/install_generated_plugin use.

force.description: Forces the hub's VS Code Remote setup (installing missing packages, configuring the environment) to run again even if it already succeeded before. Use when the customer explicitly asks to redo VS Code Remote setup, or reports problems with it. Defaults to false.

confirm_vscode_remote.description: Only pass this on a follow-up call, after this tool returned needs_confirmation: true asking whether to set up VS Code Remote and the human answered. true if they said yes, false if they said no. Omit on every other call.
